title: Katniss and Peeta Return for Haymitch's Big Moment
summary:
Spoiler warning! If you have not seen The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping yet, you may want to stop here. The big-screen prequel brings back two very familiar faces for its ending — Katniss Everdeen and Peeta Mellark.

We have known for some time that Jennifer Lawrence's Katniss and Josh Hutcherson's Peeta would return in the film. If you have read the book, you know they come back for an epilogue. In late October 2026, Lawrence confirmed that Woody Harrelson, who plays the older Haymitch Abernathy in the original films, is part of the scene too.

There are some differences between the book's epilogue and the film, directed by Francis Lawrence, but the heart of it is the same. After we watch Haymitch win his games — and see how the Capitol punishes him for fighting back against the 50th Games arena — Harrelson's Haymitch walks up to an ivy-covered structure: the old site of the annual reaping, where one boy and one girl were chosen to compete in the deadly Games.

There he is joined by Katniss and Peeta, who wish him a happy birthday. It is a major plot point in Sunrise that reaping day always falls on Haymitch's birthday. They thank him for everything, and Haymitch says "Nevermore" before departing.

It makes sense for the three of them to close out Haymitch's story together. During the original Hunger Games timeline, they are, for all intents and purposes, a package deal. The film gives the trio a hopeful, optimistic ending — though in the books, author Suzanne Collins takes a darker approach. The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping is in theaters now.
why_it_matters: For fans of the series, seeing the three heroes together closes Haymitch's story — and the film's hopeful ending gives the prequel a different feel from the books.

background_read: The Hunger Games is a series of books and films set in a future world where a powerful Capitol forces children from poor districts to fight in deadly Games.
A prequel is a story set before the original one, and Sunrise on the Reaping tells the story of a young Haymitch Abernathy winning his Games.
An epilogue is a short section at the end of a story that shows what happens later.
The reaping is the event where one boy and one girl from each district are chosen to compete in the Games.
